title: Dynamic filters by user, permission and data scope

videos.script: In lesson 2, a support agent asked when an order is held for fraud review, and got the threshold the finance team had asked to keep from agents. {{roles}} The fix starts with one question: who is asking? A customer, an agent and someone from finance ask the same thing, and each is answered from what they may read. {{where}} The filter goes inside the search. Filter after it, and the agent's three sources become two. {{rls}} Then the database enforces it too. The assistant connects with a role of its own, and a policy on the table hides every row its reader may not see, even from a query that forgot the filter. {{index}} With a vector index, a strict filter can return fewer rows than asked for. {{narrow}} A reader can narrow what they search, never widen it. {{audit}} Then a test: five roles, thirty-six questions, nine hundred rows, and not one outside its role. {{delete}} And deleting a document means its chunks are gone the same day, with a test that proves it. {{end}}
